senses.definition: (intransitive) To creep; to move slowly on hands and knees, or by dragging the body along the ground.
examples: Clutching my wounded side, I crawled back to the trench.

quotes.text: A VVorm finds vvhat it ſearches after, only by Feeling, as it cravvls from one thing to another. VVhereas a Man, having Eyes, ſees it in a Moment, all before him.

quotes.text: 'Children crawled over each other like little grey worms in the gutters,' he said. 'The only red things about them were their buttocks and they were raw. senses.definition: (intransitive) To move forward slowly, with frequent stops.
examples: The rush-hour traffic crawled around the bypass.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To act in a servile manner.
examples: Don’t come crawling to me with your useless apologies!

quotes.text: Our hard-ruled king. Again, there is sprung up. An heretic, an arch one, Cranmer; one. Hath crawled into the favour of the king

senses.definition: (intransitive) Followed by with: see crawl with.

examples: The horrible sight made my skin crawl.

senses.definition: (intransitive, transitive) To swim using the crawl stroke.
examples: I think I’ll crawl the next hundred metres.

senses.definition: (transitive) To move over (an area) on hands and knees.
examples: The baby crawled the entire second floor.

senses.definition: (transitive) To move over (an area) slowly, with frequent stops.

senses.definition: (transitive, Internet) To visit files or web sites in order to index them for searching.
examples: Yahoo Search has updated its Slurp Crawler to crawl websites faster and more efficiently.

senses.definition: The act of moving slowly on hands and knees, etc.
The act of sequentially visiting a series of similar establishments (i.e., a bar crawl).
A rapid swimming stroke with alternate overarm strokes and a fluttering kick.

examples: My computer has slowed down to a crawl since I installed that software package.
